source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed electrical appliance safety checks

1. Start with the test records.
2.
completion:
Write the date of inspection.
3. Record the appliance ID or serial number.
4. Specify the make and model of the appliance.
5. Note the name and contact information of the inspector.
6. Document the location of the appliance.
7. Record the reason for the safety check if it was not routine (e.g., report of a malfunction).
8. State the safety checks performed (e.g., visual inspection, plug checks, earth continuity, insulation resistance).
9. Detail any observed defects or damage using clear and concise language (e.g., "Cut in cable near the plug", "Discoloration on the plug, indicative of overheating").
10. Indicate whether the appliance passed or failed the check.
11. Write specific details about the failure, referencing what portion of the test caused the failure (e.g., "Failed earth continuity test" or "Insulation resistance below minimum threshold").
12. If relevant, document any warnings or error
